newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senate panel backs oil reserve for 3 years.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senate panel backs oil reserve for 3 years.

text.p: The U.S. Senate Energy Committee Wednesday approved a bill to continue the Strategic Petroleum Reserve for three years, and meet U.S. obligations to the International Energy Agency for another five years.
Committee chairman Sen. Frank Murkowski, an Alaska Republican, had wanted to extend the life of the SPR, currently authorized through September, for five years.
But the Clinton administration sought a renewal for only one year while it completed a study on the future of the oil reserve.
Murkowski compromised by reducing his proposed reauthorization to three years, and said he expected the full Senate to pass the legislation.

The bill also called for the Energy Department to use any money it receives from leasing excess storage space in SPR caverns to buy oil for the reserve beginning in the 2003 fiscal year, a committee spokesman said.
